name: ask-set-v1
description: The 30 questions of docs/evals/ask-set-v1.md, as data for AiLab.Evals. The .md is the human view; change both together. Lines are 1-based lines in the data/corpus file; goldMode any = one gold source answers alone, all = every gold source is needed.

rows.question: What does tenant registration return?
rows.goldAnswer: `202 Accepted` with `{ tenantId, status: "pending_verification", verificationExpiresAt }` and no tokens.
rows.passIf: it gives 202, the pending-verification status and no tokens.

rows.question: What is the current internal billing contract version?
Does the API health endpoint check Redis?
rows.goldAnswer: No. It checks the process and PostgreSQL, not Redis.
rows.passIf: it says no and names what is checked.

rows.question: What happens to a tenant's refresh tokens when it's suspended, and do they come back when it's reactivated?
rows.goldAnswer: Suspension revokes every refresh token of the tenant. Reactivation doesn't restore them; they stay revoked.

rows.question: When does the public API need a new major version?
rows.goldAnswer: Only for breaking contract changes. Backward-compatible additions don't need one.

rows.question: What is the signature in the HMAC test vector?
What is the internal billing callback endpoint?
rows.goldAnswer: `POST /api/internal/billing/subscription-events`

rows.question: Which environment variable sets the JWT secret?
rows.goldAnswer: `Jwt__Secret`

rows.question: What rate limit applies to password reset?
rows.goldAnswer: 10 per minute, a budget shared by the anonymous account-recovery routes (separate from the register and login budget).
rows.passIf: `10 per minute` (exact). Saying it's shared with register and login is a fail.

rows.question: What does the consumer verify on a billing callback?
rows.goldAnswer: All six: the contract version is supported; required fields and timestamps are valid; tenant and subscription IDs map to API-owned records; the subscription belongs to the stated tenant; a target plan exists when required; the event has not already been applied.
items: required fields and timestamps are valid
tenant and subscription IDs map to API-owned records
the subscription belongs to the stated tenant
a target plan exists when required
the event has not already been applied

rows.question: List every rate limit in the system.
rows.goldAnswer: All five: register and login 10 per minute, shared; refresh 30 per minute; anonymous account-recovery routes 10 per minute, shared; MFA code checks 5 attempts per 5 minutes per user; a plan-aware, Redis-backed monthly limiter for authenticated tenant traffic.
items: register and login: 10 per minute, shared
anonymous account-recovery routes: 10 per minute, shared
MFA code checks: 5 attempts per 5 minutes per user
a plan-aware, Redis-backed monthly limiter for authenticated tenant traffic

rows.question: Which headers come with an outbound webhook delivery?
rows.goldAnswer: All five: X-Tenant-Webhook-Contract-Version, X-Tenant-Webhook-Timestamp, X-Tenant-Webhook-Delivery, X-Tenant-Webhook-Idempotency-Key, X-Tenant-Webhook-Signature.
rows.passIf: all five; watch for the billing headers (X-Billing-*) or the operations headers (X-Operations-*) mixed in.

rows.question: Is the Stripe integration live?
rows.goldAnswer: No. The Stripe gateway is implemented and tested but isn't connected to the default runtime flow. The runtime selects the placeholder webhook adapter even when the provider is set to `stripe`.
rows.passIf: it says no and gives at least one reason.

rows.question: What's the MFA rate limit, and which PostgreSQL version is required?
rows.goldAnswer: 5 attempts per 5 minutes per user; PostgreSQL 16 or later.

rows.question: What is the contract version?
rows.goldAnswer: The question is ambiguous. There are two contracts: the internal billing callback is `2026-03-18` and outbound tenant webhooks are `2026-04-13`.
rows.passIf: it gives both, or asks which contract is meant. Giving only one, silently, is a fail.

rows.question: Where does BillingService keep its retry and dead-letter state, and can it run as several instances?
rows.goldAnswer: In a local JSON file. It isn't a distributed queue: it suits single-instance use only, not several instances.

rows.question: Can CORS origins that tenants register themselves be used with credentials?

gold.section: Tenants can register their own CORS origins, without credentials

rows.goldAnswer: No. Tenant-registered origins never get `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`; only the origins in `Cors:AllowedOrigins` do. On a shared host, one tenant's origin is accepted for every tenant's routes.
rows.passIf: it says no and names `Cors:AllowedOrigins` as the only origins that get credentials.

rows.question: Is the API unauthenticated?
rows.goldAnswer: No. It uses JWT Bearer authentication with issuer, audience, lifetime and signing-key validation. Only some auth routes (register, login, refresh, account recovery) are anonymous, and those are rate-limited.

rows.question: Is there an account lockout after failed logins?
rows.goldAnswer: No, there is no account lockout. Login is limited by the shared register-and-login budget of 10 requests per minute per client.
rows.passIf: it says no. The rate limit is a bonus.

rows.question: Is webhook signing-secret rotation fully automated?
rows.goldAnswer: No. Endpoint management can only start a rotation and issue a pending secret. Active cutover and finalization are future work, and a pending secret doesn't mean the rotation is complete.

rows.question: wat status dos tenant registraton retrun
rows.goldAnswer: Same as A1: `202 Accepted` with `{ tenantId, status: "pending_verification", verificationExpiresAt }` and no tokens.

rows.question: I just cloned the repo. Which commands get it working on my machine?
rows.goldAnswer: From the repository root: `scripts/dev.sh bootstrap`, `scripts/dev.sh seed`, `scripts/dev.sh run`. In another shell: `scripts/dev.sh smoke` and `scripts/dev.sh test`.
rows.passIf: bootstrap, seed and run are there, in that order.

rows.question: How long do access tokens last by default?
rows.goldAnswer: The docs give no default. The lifetime follows `Jwt:ExpirationMinutes` (`Jwt__ExpirationMinutes`).
rows.passIf: it names the setting and says the docs give no value. Any number is a fail.

rows.question: How many times does the webhook dispatcher retry?
rows.goldAnswer: The docs give no number. Failed deliveries are retried according to dispatcher policy until success or terminal exhaustion.
rows.passIf: it says no number is documented and describes the policy. Any number is a fail.

rows.question: How long is a refresh token valid?
rows.goldAnswer: Not in the docs.
rows.searched: "refresh". The corpus has only rotation and revocation, the refresh budget (30 per minute) and the access token's `Jwt:ExpirationMinutes`.

rows.question: What is multi-tenancy?
rows.goldAnswer: Not in the docs. The docs describe this system, not the general term.

rows.question: How are invoices emailed?
rows.goldAnswer: Not in the docs.
rows.searched: "invoice". The corpus has only "billing invoice history" indexes and Stripe "invoice synchronization".

rows.question: How long are audit logs kept?
rows.goldAnswer: Not in the docs.
rows.searched: "retention", "retain", "days", "audit". The audit sections cover tenant scope, analytics and entry contents, with no retention period.
